facts.statement: Gettyia is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird belonging to the family Avisauridae that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Gettyia is an extinct genus of avisaurid enantiornithean bird from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: The species was originally described as Avisaurus gloriae in 1995 based on a single tarsometatarsus fossil found in Glacier County, Montana.
facts.quote: Gettyia was originally named Avisaurus gloriae by Varrichio and Chiappe (1995) for MOR 553E/6.19.91.64, a tarsometatarsus from the late Campanian Upper Two Medicine Formation of Glacier County, Montana, USA.

facts.statement: The specific name gloriae honors Gloria Siebrecht, a volunteer fossil collector who discovered the original specimen.
facts.quote: The species name honors Gloria Siebrecht, a volunteer fossil collector at the Museum of the Rockies who discovered the specimen.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gettyia date to the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Gettyia was originally named Avisaurus gloriae by Varrichio and Chiappe (1995) for MOR 553E/6.19.91.64, a tarsometatarsus from the late Campanian Upper Two Medicine Formation of Glacier County, Montana, USA.

facts.statement: Gettyia lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gettyia inhabited both humid low-lying swamps near the Western Interior Seaway and the drier uplands leading to the Rocky Mountains.
facts.quote: Gettyia is known from the humid low-lying swamps, lakes, and river basins of the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, and from the much more arid uplands between that area and the Cordilleran Overthrust Belt which eventually formed the Rocky Mountains.

facts.statement: Gettyia is known from a single fossilized right tarsometatarsus bone.
facts.quote: Gettyia is known from a single right tarsometatarsus.

facts.statement: The known bone of Gettyia is similar to those of other North American avisaurids but is much smaller in size.
facts.quote: This bone was similar to that of other North American avisaurids such as Avisaurus and Mirarce, but it was much smaller.

facts.statement: Gettyia possessed a knob-like structure on the front edge of its second metatarsal that connected to the tibialis cranialis muscle.
facts.quote: The second metatarsal had a tubercule (knob-like structure) on its front edge, which likely connected to the tibialis cranialis muscle which flexes the ankle.

facts.statement: The third and fourth metatarsals of Gettyia were more extensively fused than in other avisaurids, with fusion occurring near both the ankle and the toes.
facts.quote: The third and fourth metatarsals are more extensively fused than in other avisaurids, as fusion occurs not only near the ankle, but also near the toes.

facts.statement: The position of the tibialis cranialis tubercule suggests that Gettyia had a more specialized lifestyle than other avisaurids.
facts.quote: The more distally placed tibialis cranialis tubercule of Gettyia suggests that it had a more specialized lifestyle compared to other avisaurids.

facts.statement: Birds of prey utilize forceful flexion during their hunting behavior.
facts.quote: Birds of prey in particular utilize forceful flexion during their hunting behavior.

facts.statement: Arboreal parrots and climbing birds use forceful flexion to maintain stability while foraging or hanging from branches.
facts.quote: Arboreal parrots and other climbing birds also make use of forceful flexion to obtain stability while foraging or hanging from tree branches.

facts.statement: More terrestrial birds typically require speed over force to assist with locomotion like walking and hopping.
facts.quote: More terrestrial birds typically need more speed and less force, to assist locomotion like walking and hopping.

facts.statement: Gettyia is classified within the family Avisauridae.
The genus Gettyia was established by Atterholt and colleagues in 2018.
Gettyia is an extinct genus of avialan belonging to the clade Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Gettyia es un género extinto de avialano perteneciente al clado Enantiornithes que habitó Norteamérica durante el Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: Gettyia is a monotypic genus known only from the species G. gloriae.
facts.quote: Es un género monotípico conocido a partir de la especie G. gloriae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Gettyia is the family Avisauridae.
